factChecks.claim: Apple's Foundation Models framework exposes guided generation, streaming, tool calling, and stateful sessions around its on-device model.
Apple describes its device-scale model as optimized for tasks including summarization, extraction, and classification, not world knowledge or advanced reasoning.
On-device models change which AI features can reasonably be integrated into everyday app workflows.

angle: guided generation turns model output into data a Swift app can use
shareValue: A concrete travel-app example showing why typed model output is more useful than unstructured prose.
problemStatement: Unstructured model prose is difficult and fragile for an app to parse into interface data.
solutionStatement: Guided Generation lets the developer request a defined Swift type that can map directly into the interface.

verifiedFacts: The framework provides access to the on-device language model behind Apple Intelligence.
Apple documents guided generation into Swift data structures, streaming, tool calling, and stateful sessions.
editorialBrief.analysis: The important product question is not whether AI can generate text, but whether it removes a real decision, drafting, or organization burden inside the workflow.
doNotClaim: Do not call every interaction private or offline.
Do not claim model accuracy, speed, or availability beyond the source.

captions.instagram:
A language model writes text. Your app usually needs usable data.

Apple’s Guided Generation addresses that gap. In Apple’s travel-app example, the developer defines a SearchSuggestions Swift type, asks the model to generate it, and receives a structured object that can map directly to the interface.

The practical result: instead of prompting for JSON and repairing unexpected formatting, the app requests the shape it needs—four search suggestions—and renders those results as UI.

This approach fits narrow, repeatable tasks where predictable structure matters. Apple says its device-scale model is suited to work such as summarization, extraction, and classification—not world knowledge or advanced reasoning.

Source: Apple Developer, Meet the Foundation Models framework (WWDC25)
